task: Correct memory_enhancement CLI documentation to the measured command surface and install an executable guard

events.content: Built an executable guard that parses every documented memory_enhancement invocation against the real argparse parser, with negative and positive controls.
A self-written control caught the detector mistaking a global option value for a subcommand name; added _VALUE_TAKING_GLOBALS and a dedicated control.
Read confidence.py, verification.py, health.py, and serena_integration.py to establish the measured formulas and citation source types.
Built probe repositories and captured real CLI output for every documented example instead of inventing output.
Rewrote SKILL.md, confidence-scoring.md, examples.md, CITATION-SCHEMA.md, and the reflect Phase 4 section against measured behavior.
Proved citations parse inline but links are dropped unless they end their line, and that an unrecognized source type drops the citation while the memory still exits 0.
Rewrote memory-citation-guide.md from 378 lines to 150, removing a duplicated and fabricated schema in favour of a pointer to CITATION-SCHEMA.md.
Confirmed via git history that the issue-998 memory was accurate when written and superseded by PR 1576; annotated rather than rewrote the record.
Widened the guard to bare subcommand fragments; the new controls exposed a pre-existing normalizer bug where the '>' closing a placeholder was treated as a shell redirect.
Regenerated the Copilot CLI skill mirrors with build/scripts/generate_skills.py and bumped both project-toolkit manifests to 0.6.5431.

Ran two adversarial review rounds on other model families; reproduced every finding by execution before acting, which downgraded two of seven from one reviewer and rejected one of three from the other.

Closed four scanner holes the reviews found: an int substitution swallowing the following flag, a line continuation hiding a flag, a redirect leaving a stray descriptor, and exempt roots deletable without detection.

Rejected a fifth proposed widening after measuring corpus incidence: the single command substitution in the corpus is quoted and already parses, and the unquoted form fails loudly rather than silently.
Mutation-tested three new assertions by reverting each fix in turn and confirming the matching test fails; guard suite is 71 tests, up from 63.

Disproved my own correction: a probe showed a TypeScript file containing the comment '// def ts_func' verifies as PASS, so the citation check is a raw text search, not a definition check, and all three documents now say that.
All three confirmed. Pinned utf-8 with errors=replace, normalized three module paths to memory_enhancement, and recorded the ending commit.
Single spelling of record across every document that describes the CLI.
Found a defect class the guard misses entirely: it validates flag syntax but never argument values.
Left examples.md alone. Changing it would have broken a deliberate teaching fixture.
A hypothetical is unavoidable in CITATION-SCHEMA.md, so declared it in prose instead of inventing a fake id.
Guard 71 passed, 0 em or en dashes across all changed files, no .claude changes so no version bump or mirror regeneration required.
